ops.title: kg persistence seam: build writes, stat and query read, a miss is loud and never persisted
ops.body:
`Index.Graph() (*Graph, bool)` exists in `internal/kg/index.go` because without it the Save/Load layer is dead code exercised only by kg's own tests: `rank.New`, `Enrich` and `newGraphLane` all take a `*kg.Graph`, so `kg query` could never read a stored index at all, and the "node and edge counts by kind" criterion is unreachable from a load. It decodes all four buckets back into a `*kg.Graph` and re-sorts edges into `Graph`'s documented (from, kind, to) order — the bbolt forward key is (from, to, kind). Round-trip pinned by `TestIndexGraphRoundTripsTheBuiltGraph`.

Miss semantics, chosen deliberately rather than inherited:

- `kg build` is the only writer. It calls `ccnhome.RecordWorktree`, saves into `<root>/repos/<key>/graph-v1`, then re-`Load`s to verify the write landed — `kg.Save` is best-effort with no error return, so without the re-read the command would report a persistence that never happened.
- `kg stat` and `kg query` call `kg.Load` with `kg.SourceDigest`. The outcome is named in the `index` field (`hit` / `miss` / `written`), a miss is announced on stderr, folded in process to answer, and discarded. A read never persists. `kg.Load` treats every deviation as a miss by construction, so there is no partial-index state to reason about.

Why it matters downstream: Phase 4's hooks read through this surface, and the reason `kg query` reads the stored graph rather than rebuilding is exactly that the rebuild is what the daemon exists to amortize.

Related: the graph lives under the per-user root, never in the git dir and never on `refs/cc-notes/*` — a derived artifact that rebuilds in under a second is a cache, not a correctness surface.
